Among West Virginia’s 55 counties, Wyoming County comes in 28th for residents age 65 and up (4,824). Older adults make up 23.8% of the population here; the state figure is 21.5%. The 1,387 residents now between 60 and 64 will become Medicare-eligible soon, and our turning 65 guide walks through it. By age, the 65-and-older group splits 64% ages 65 to 74, 29% ages 75 to 84 and 8% age 85 and up (Census 2023). Medicare Advantage enrollment in Wyoming County is 68.5% of people with Medicare, higher than the West Virginia average of 56.6%. What most people do in a county is less important than what fits you. We weigh Medicare Advantage against Original Medicare with Medigap using your doctors, your drugs and your budget.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Who has Medicare in Wyoming County

Wyoming County is a rural county; the U.S. Department of Agriculture describes it as: urban population of fewer than 5,000, adjacent to a metro area. Rural counties tend to have fewer local hospitals and doctors, so a plan’s network and the distance to care matter a great deal.

CMS counts 6,088 Medicare beneficiaries in Wyoming County (2023). Their average age is 68, younger than the West Virginia average of 72. About 31% are “dual eligible,” meaning they have both Medicare and Medicaid, higher than the state figure of 20%. Where many people have both, special plans for dual-eligible members can matter; see our Medicaid and dual eligible guide, since availability varies by plan and area.

Among people in Original Medicare in Wyoming County, CMS reported about 693 emergency room visits and 309 inpatient hospital stays per 1,000 beneficiaries in 2023, which is close to the state average for emergency visits (684) and higher than it for hospital stays (250). About 8% received home health care. These figures describe how people use care under Original Medicare; they do not show what any plan covers or costs.

Sources: CMS Medicare Geographic Variation, 2023; USDA Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, 2023.

Where you live decides which Medicare Advantage and Part D plans you can join, and Wyoming County may have a different set of plans than the counties around it. We are not based in Wyoming County; we help Wyoming County residents by phone or video call.

Hospitals and doctors near Wyoming County

CMS Hospital General Information lists no acute care, critical access or children’s hospital located inside Wyoming County. Residents often use hospitals in neighboring counties, which matters for Medicare Advantage because a plan’s network may include or leave out the hospital you use. We check your hospitals and doctors before you enroll.

Where people live in Wyoming County

People in Wyoming County live in communities such as Oceana (1,389), Mullens (1,383), Pineville (610) (2023 population estimates, counting only the part of each community that lies inside the county).

We look up plans by ZIP code. In Wyoming County, that means areas such as 24716, 24719, 24726, 24736, 24801, 24818, 24822, 24823, 24827, 24834, 24839, 24845, 24847, 24849 and 22 more, based on Census ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that lie mostly in the county.

Common questions

Wyoming County Medicare FAQ

Can I get help with Medicare in Wyoming County by phone?
Yes. Phone and video appointments are how we serve Wyoming County. We hold a West Virginia license, compare plans from many carriers and walk you through them from home, with no pressure to enroll.
Will my Wyoming County doctors and hospitals be covered?
On a Medicare Advantage plan it depends on that plan’s network, so before you enroll we check whether your doctors and the hospitals you use are in network, including hospitals in neighboring counties. With a Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plan you can see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
How many people in Wyoming County have Medicare Advantage?
CMS reported 3,721 people enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan out of 5,433 people with Medicare in Wyoming County in September 2026, or 68.5%. The West Virginia average was 56.6%.
Do you charge Wyoming County residents for help?
No, there is no fee. The insurance company pays us when you enroll, and your premium does not go up because you used an agent.
When can I enroll or change plans?
You can enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event such as moving into or within the county.
